summary: Master humanitarian financial monitoring, donor compliance, and IPSAS reporting. Learn to manage BVA, fraud risks, and digital cash for aid organizations.
lede: Financial Monitoring and Reporting in Humanitarian Settings helps professionals track, analyze, and report on aid funds while strengthening accountability, efficiency, and donor trust. The course develops practical skills in multi-currency accounting, indirect cost recovery, internal controls, budget variance analysis, procurement tracking, and cash flow forecasting. Through practical simulation and compliance mapping, you will learn to prioritize high-risk transactions, support partner due diligence, and manage challenges such as limited connectivity and fluctuating exchange rates. You will also explore digital finance tools and AI-assisted fraud detection patterns to turn financial data into a stronger resource for program decisions.
audienceIntro: This training is essential for professionals who manage, report on, or audit financial resources within the humanitarian and international development sectors.
modules: Humanitarian Finance Landscape and IPSAS Standards
Budget Variance Analysis and Financial Monitoring
Cash and Liquidity Management in Field Operations
Digital Finance and AI in Humanitarian Monitoring
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 2-3 years of experience in finance, accounting, or grant management within a non-profit or humanitarian organization. Familiarity with basic budgeting and Excel is required. Knowledge of specific donor regulations (e.g., USAID, ECHO) is beneficial but not mandatory.
